papers.title: Single-cell Transcriptomics and Proteomic Imaging of Tumor- and Non-hematopoietic Signal-associated Hematopoietic Bias and Immune Suppression in Metastatic Bone Marrow.
papers.authors: Shen Z, Wang P, Xu G, Yuan H, Jiang H, Shi J, Xiao J, Xu W.
papers.abstract: Bone metastases profoundly alter the bone marrow microenvironment; however, the mechanisms by which metastatic tumors reprogram hematopoiesis and immune organization across distinct marrow regions remain incompletely understood. Here, we generate a pan-cancer single-cell atlas comprising 212,565 cells by integrating bone marrow specimens from breast, bile duct, colorectal, esophageal, renal, lung, prostate, and thyroid cancers, together with benign controls, delineating nine major lineages and 61 cellular subpopulations. This analysis reveals coordinated immune suppression and niche remodeling, marked by contraction of hematopoietic progenitors, innate NK cells, and adaptive T and B cells, concomitant with expansion of myeloid, stromal, and epithelial compartments. We further characterize cancer-specific stromal distribution patterns, epithelial transcriptional programs, and accompanying alterations in hematopoietic signaling pathways, including ICAM- and ADGRE-associated interactions. Hematopoietic output is redirected toward myelopoiesis, exhibiting a lineage bias at the Granulocyte-Monocyte Progenitor (GMP) stage. Cell-cell communication analysis suggests potential interactions between hematopoietic progenitors and exhaustion-associated T-cell populations, including the LGALS9-HAVCR2 axis. Spatial proteomic comparison of three anatomical regions from a single patient with lung cancer and benign marrow from 12 donors reveals GMP-T-cell co-localization in both settings, with increased neighborhood enrichment restricted to the tumor-marrow interface in the patient examined. Collectively, these findings provide an integrated transcriptional and spatial proteomic framework for interpreting the metastatic marrow ecosystem through the convergence of stromal disruption, hematopoietic reprogramming, and immune dysfunction.

papers.title: Deep Learning-Guided Design of Candidate Synthetic Cis-Regulatory Elements for a TCF7+ Progenitor-Exhausted-like CD8+ T-Cell State
papers.authors: Buhn, N.; Lee, M.; Kim, D.; Gill, S.
papers.abstract: Progenitor-exhausted CD8+ T cells (Tex-prog) are essential for sustaining T-cell-mediated immunity during chronic infection and cancer and therefore offer a promising immunotherapy target. Synthetic cis-regulatory elements (CREs) could enable selective transgene expression in Tex-prog cells, but whether they can distinguish this population from closely related CD8+ T-cell exhaustion states remains unclear. Here, we integrated publicly available paired single-cell ATAC-seq and single-cell RNA-seq datasets from mouse infection and tumor models and identified an ATAC-defined Tex-prog-like population (C1). We used the CREsted framework to fine-tune a pretrained Borzoi model to predict chromatin accessibility across C1 and ten comparator populations. We then used CREsted to design candidate synthetic CREs with predicted preferential accessibility in C1. The fine-tuned model achieved an average precision of 0.242 for identifying C1-selective regions on chromosomes held out from fine-tuning, approximately tenfold higher than the random-ranking baseline. Sequence optimization generated 196 1,000-bp designs with at least twofold higher predicted accessibility in C1 relative to the strongest competing population across eight DNA backgrounds. Motif enrichment and sequence-attribution analyses identified sequence patterns associated with AP-1, NFAT, POU, EGR, and TCF/LEF transcription factor families. Together, these findings identify candidate synthetic CREs with predicted preferential accessibility in a Tex-prog-like CD8+ T-cell population and provide a foundation for future experimental evaluation of their functional enhancer activity and cell-state specificity.

papers.title: Human Lung Mast cell Diversity Across Anatomical Compartments Defined by Single-Cell Transcriptomics
papers.authors: Gong, Y.; Atanasoai, I.; Boey, D.; Johnsson, A.-K.; Al-Ameri, M.; Sachs, E.; Vali, K.; Adner, M.; Dahlen, S.-E.; Säfholm, J.; Dahlin, J. S.; Nilsson, G. P.; Rönnberg, E.
papers.abstract: Background: Mast cells are key regulators of inflammatory lung diseases, including asthma. Yet, the heterogeneity of lung mast cells and their specialization in different lung compartments remain poorly defined. Traditional protease-based classifications fail to capture distinct mast cell states relevant to airway pathology, highlighting the need for high-resolution, compartment-resolved analyses. Objective: To determine the heterogeneity of human lung mast cells in different lung compartments. Methods: We performed single-cell RNA sequencing analysis of human lung mast cells from four anatomical compartments; bronchi, parenchyma, arteries and veins. Bioinformatical analysis was used to characterize mast cell heterogeneity and compartment-specific specialization. Results: Five transcriptional distinct mast cell states (MC1-MC5) were identified. MC1 was characterized by stress response (e.g., MT2A, MRPL14, SNN), MC2 by broad immediate-early gene activation (e.g., FOS, JUN), and MC3 by a more selective activation with TGF-{beta} response enrichment. MC4 displayed a pro-inflammatory effector phenotype enriched for IL-33-responses (e.g., CCL2, CCL4, CCL4L2, IL13), consistent with roles in airway inflammation. MC5 was associated with long non-coding RNAs (MEG3, MEG8). Mast cell states showed anatomical segregation with inflammatory cytokines enriched in bronchial and arterial mast cells while reduced in parenchymal mast cells. We further identified MCTC-like mast cells co-expressing CTSG, CMA1 and ADCYAP1, characterized by enhanced metabolic programming. Conclusions: This study provides a comprehensive single-cell transcriptomic atlas of human lung mast cells, revealing five distinct transcriptional states and compartment-specific functional specialization. These findings link mast cell heterogeneity to airway inflammation and provide a translational framework for targeting mast cells in lung diseases.

papers.title: Robust single-cell analysis through subsampling reveals hidden naive T cell states in aging
papers.authors: Rahmani, E.; Alber, S.; Reich-Zeliger, S.; Mark, M.; Etxezarreta Arrastoa, O.; Ergen, C.; Wagner, A.; Benuck, E.; Avram, O.; Song, Y. S.; Quintana, F. J.; Anderson, A. C.; Chavdarova, T.; Jordan, M. I.; Wang, Y.; Yosef, N.
papers.abstract: Single-cell genomics has been instrumental for studying the variation between cell states. Yet, the use of single-cell technologies to study variation between sample groups remains challenging, with findings often failing to replicate across cohorts. Here, we introduce a general framework for robust single-cell analysis that uses subsampling of individuals to identify statistical patterns that hold regardless of which unmeasured characteristics of those individuals covary with the condition of interest. Within this framework, a t-test for differential expression, a chi-squared test for differential composition, and a linear projection for contrastive representation learning outperform state-of-the-art alternatives in cross-cohort replicability. This identifies robustness by design, rather than refined distributional assumptions and model expressiveness, as a principal driver of reproducible discovery in single-cell studies. Applying robust contrastive learning to naive CD4 T cells from human blood, we uncover eleven replicating age-associated subpopulations, largely uncharacterized, that express programs of other states and go undetected by standard analysis. One of them is most strongly defined by CTLA4, a checkpoint receptor considered a hallmark of antigen-experienced and regulatory T cells, yet carries a naive surface phenotype and is distinct from regulatory T cells. This population is conserved in mice and increases in frequency with age in both the CD4 and CD8 compartments. Upon stimulation, these cells exhibit attenuated proliferation compared with conventional naive T cells and enrichment of regulatory phenotypes. Blocking CTLA4 signaling largely restores the downstream activation program to that of conventional naive cells, suggesting these cells may be a reversible contributor to the age-associated decline in naive T-cell responsiveness. By prioritizing robustness over richer models, our framework enables discovery of previously hidden cellular heterogeneity and offers a general strategy for improving resolution and replicability in single-cell genomics. Code is available at github.com/robust-precision-medicine.

papers.title: Task-aligned foundation model representations enable single-cell cytokine response inference
papers.authors: Jeong, Y. L.; Kim, J. K.
papers.abstract: Inferring cellular responses from single-cell transcriptomes requires interpreting changes relative to an appropriate baseline while retaining cell-type context. Here we present CYTAP, which adapts frozen single-cell foundation model embeddings for cytokine-response inference by combining donor-adjusted receiver states with deviations from matched control centroids. CYTAP uses a shared classifier to assign relative single-cell response scores across 90 cytokines and supports unpaired analyses using counterfactual control references. Baseline-relative representations improved held-out-donor prediction with both State SE and scFoundation. Across independent perturbation datasets, CYTAP prioritized applied cytokines, including when receptor transcripts were sparsely detected, and ranked administered cytokines among the top ten in both in vivo datasets. In an unpaired COVID-19 cohort, inferred responses were associated with severity, and IL-6 response scores correlated with plasma IL-6 concentrations. These findings support the use of biologically defined references to adapt pretrained representations for functional response inference.

papers.title: A cross-species single-cell spatial atlas of kidney allografts
papers.authors: Wu, J.; Miao, L.; Zhao, Y.; Chen, S.; Shi, R.; Yu, B.; Lu, Z.; Wang, C.; Song, X.; Yu, X.; Rong, R.; Yang, C.; Shang, G.; Zhu, T.; Zhu, D.
papers.abstract: Kidney allografts with the same Banff diagnosis differ in their immune microenvironments and functional recovery after treatment, yet the tissue features distinguishing recovery from non-recovery remain unclear. We constructed SPECTRA (Spatial Etiology and Coordination of Transplant Rejection in Allografts), which comprises spatial multi-omic data from 1,011,984 cells in 83 human allograft biopsies. We also profiled 442,320 cells from 34 mouse grafts across experimental groups and time points by single-cell sequencing, and integrated a public human single-cell reference of 352,911 cells. Unsupervised analysis identified nine tissue niches, of which plasma-cell effector niche occupancy was associated with less eGFR improvement approximately 90 days after biopsy ({rho} = -0.508, q = 0.0165). Plasma cells in this niche expressed IGHG1, IGKC and TXNDC5; in scarred interstitium, plasma-cell XBP1, HSPA5 and SEC61A1 expression increased with fibrosis. Tertiary lymphoid structures retained TCF7-high stem-like T cells that received CCL19-CCR7 signals from fibroblasts. Using multimodal deep-learning models to delineate anatomical regions, we separated Banff lesions into local immune-load and chronic morphological-injury axes, each with distinct compartmental responses. Peritubular-capillary endothelium increased interferon-{gamma}-associated antigen presentation with local immune load, glomerular endothelium reduced MHC expression with glomerular inflammation, and chronic injury was accompanied by reduced metabolic programmes in specific cell types. In mice, we built a single-cell atlas of kidney transplantation covering syngeneic grafts and BALB/c, DBA/2J and DBA/2N[->]C57BL/6 models. Graft trajectories separated into rejection-associated and tolerance-associated paths that differed in interferon-activated myeloid states and Hnf4a- and Ppara-associated tubular metabolism. In 20 human recipients with rejection-spectrum diagnoses, predictions of functional non-response from a hierarchical causal-inference model were most sensitive to plasma-cell niche occupancy and density. Niche maps predicted from routine H&E were associated with subsequent kidney function. These findings show that kidney allograft rejection is accompanied by changes in cellular states and spatial organisation, and identify plasma-cell niches in residual and scarred interstitium as tissue features of functional non-recovery after rejection.

papers.title: Structural Landscape of MHC Complexes through Fold Mining
papers.authors: de Lima, G. S.; dos Santos, P. H. A.; de Assis, S. C.; Nazare, P. G. B. d. S.; Simoes, C. D. M. S.; Chaves, E. J. F.; Jara, G. E.; Maidana, R. L. B. R.; Ribeiro-Filho, H. V.
papers.abstract: Major histocompatibility complex (MHC) proteins share a characteristic structural platform formed by two -helices positioned above a {beta}-sheet (1-2 domain), which can accommodate ligands and provide an exposed surface for recognition by protein binding partners. This interaction system is best characterized for classical MHC-I molecules presenting peptides to T-cell receptors (TCRs), one of the most extensively studied mechanisms of immune recognition. However, non-classical MHC and MHC-like proteins reveal that the 1-2 platform is considerably more versatile, supporting a remarkably diverse range of biological functions. Related architectures are also exploited by pathogens, further expanding the diversity of molecular interactions associated with this fold. Yet how this functional diversity relates to structural variation within the shared 1-2 platform and to the diverse modes of recognition employed by natural and engineered binding partners has not been systematically examined across the broader MHC fold. Here, we systematically mapped MHC 1-2-like domains across experimentally determined structures in the Protein Data Bank and predicted structures in the AlphaFold Protein Structure Database using Foldseek, and compiled their natural and engineered binding partners. Our comparative analyses revealed substantial heterogeneity across multiple structural layers, including 1-2 geometry, ligand-binding cavity architecture, and the physicochemical properties and spatial conservation of exposed recognition surfaces, despite the overall conservation of the fold. We further characterized a diverse repertoire of natural and engineered binding partners, revealing distinct structural architectures, interface compositions, and recognition geometries. Together, these findings provide an integrated structural landscape connecting the diversity of the MHC fold with the multiple modes of molecular recognition it supports, offering a comparative framework for understanding these interactions and guiding the engineering of novel MHC-targeting proteins.

papers.title: Targeting bromodomain plant homeodomain finger transcription factor reverses melanoma immune evasion via the p53/PD‑L1 axis: A study integrating machine learning identification and methapyrilene repurposing.
papers.authors: Kang X, He J, Yao X, Zhang X, Shen B, Yang J.
papers.abstract: Primary non‑response and acquired resistance limit immunotherapy efficacy in melanoma. Tumor‑cell transcriptional programs influence immune‑checkpoint signaling and susceptibility to T cell‑mediated killing. The present study aimed to identify actionable tumor‑intrinsic regulators of immune escape and evaluate their therapeutic tractability. Transcriptomic data from four melanoma immunotherapy datasets were integrated for differential expression analysis. Candidate genes were selected using three machine learning (ML) approaches. Subsequently, eight ML models and the SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis were used to prioritize response‑associated features. Pathway enrichment analysis explored biological pathways associated with the top‑ranked candidate gene. Drug‑gene interaction analysis, molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations identified therapeutic candidates. Gene overexpression and knockdown models were established by plasmid and short hairpin RNA transfection, respectively. Colony‑formation, Transwell, western blotting, cellular thermal shift, drug affinity‑responsive target stability and T‑cell co‑culture assays were performed. Six feature genes were identified. Particularly, bromodomain plant homeodomain finger transcription factor (BPTF) ranked highest and was negatively associated with immune therapy response. BPTF‑high samples demonstrated negative enrichment of the p53 pathway. In vitro , BPTF overexpression notably promoted melanoma clonogenic growth and invasion, suppressed p53 signaling, increased mouse double minute 2 (MDM2) and programmed death‑ligand 1 (PD‑L1) expression, and impaired CD8 + T‑cell activation and cytotoxicity. BPTF knockdown produced reciprocal effects. Chromatin immunoprecipitation‑quantitative PCR and dual‑luciferase assays supported BPTF‑mediated repression of TP53 and activation of CD274 . Methapyrilene demonstrated stable predicted binding to BPTF, increased BPTF thermal and proteolytic stability, and attenuated BPTF‑associated malignant and immune‑evasive phenotypes. The combination with PD‑L1 blockade enhanced tumor‑cell killing and T‑cell effector responses compared with either treatment alone. In conclusion, BPTF associates melanoma progression with immune escape through the p53/PD‑L1 axis. Methapyrilene interacts with BPTF and provides a lead scaffold for developing BPTF‑directed agents in combination with PD‑L1 blockade to overcome immunotherapy resistance in the future.

papers.title: Stk11 deficiency promotes tumor CXCL16 secretion and a CXCL16-dependent expansion of Aregpos CXCR6pos Vγ6 γδT17 in lung cancer
papers.authors: Horrigan, K. J.; Ragusa, J. M.; Mistri, S. K.; Dienz, O.; Hilton, B. M.; Lenahan, S. M.; Racela, A. R.; Deming, P. B.; Janssen-Heininger, Y. M. W.; Seward, D. J.; Poynter, M. E.; Boyson, J. E.
papers.abstract: IL-17-producing gamma delta ({gamma}{delta}T17) T cells can promote tumor growth and metastasis. How the tumor microenvironment controls the activation, expansion, and function of {gamma}{delta}T17 in different cancers remains unclear. Using an autochthonous model of KrasG12D/Stk11-driven lung adenocarcinoma coupled with scRNAseq and V(D)J profiling, we found that KrasG12DStk11-loss tumors induced a rapid expansion of lung CXCR6+ V{gamma}4 and amphiregulin-expressing CXCR6+ V{gamma}6{gamma}{delta}T17 cells. Single-cell immune profiling of the KrasG12DStk11-loss tumors revealed a prominent Krt8+ alveolar epithelial cell (KAC) tumor subtype enriched in a number of immune-relevant genes, including Cxcl16 and its sheddase Adam10, and in vitro culture revealed that KACs, but not their normal epithelial cell counterparts, secreted CXCL16. Finally, we found that in vivo blockade of CXCL16 inhibited the expansion of lung V{gamma}6+ {gamma}{delta}T17 in response to KrasG12DStk11-loss tumors. Together, these data suggest that Stk11 loss promotes a CXCL16-secreting Krt8+ KAC tumor subtype, and that CXCL16-CXCR6 interactions are necessary to drive the expansion of pro-tumor {gamma}{delta}T17 cells in lung cancer.

papers.title: Measuring and reducing segmentation-driven cell-type labeling errors in imaging spatial transcriptomics
papers.authors: Elgart, V.; Loscalzo, J.
papers.abstract: Imaging spatial transcriptomics labels each segmented cell from transcripts that include some of its neighbors RNA. We labeled each cell from its nucleus and its whole mask at equal depth, with two nuclear halves as a null. Whole-cell counts drew small, RNA-poor cells toward their larger neighbors labels. On three platforms, relative to nuclear labels at equal depth, T and NK cells lost 23-53% of their labels in six datasets of five tissues and 4-9% in renal cell carcinoma; this label-only measure matched same-cell protein markers in five donors and, where it differed, understated the loss. In gut, labels alone placed the loss at 58% of T cells among epithelial cells, compared with 24% in the lamina propria. The error lowered immune contact counts mainly by removing T cells; random relabeling, a common robustness test, raised them. Nuclear labels, where nuclei held enough counts, recovered many lost T cells. Imaged nuclei also carried some neighbor RNA and isolated nuclei carried none, indicating that these losses are lower bounds.

papers.title: Agonistic anti-CD40 monoclonal antibody improves the antitumor efficacy of a clinical chemo-immunotherapy regimen in a refractory mouse neuroblastoma model.
papers.authors: Rakhmilevich, A. L.; Matthews, J.; Felder, M. A.; Heaton, A. K.; Gao, A.; Unni, A.; Delcore, K. C.; Horwitz, B. B.; Carlisle, C.; Witt, C.; Hess, N. P.; Zaborek, J.; Skala, M.; Dinh, H.; Erbe, A. K.; Sondel, P. M.
papers.abstract: Background: The current standard regimen for relapsed-refractory high-risk neuroblastoma (HR-NB) is the combination of chemotherapy agents -Temozolomide and Irinotecan - and anti-GD2 antibody dinutuximab (TIG). This treatment results in an overall response for ~40% of patients, but the remaining 60% are resistant to TIG. We hypothesized that agonistic anti-CD40 monoclonal antibody (aCD40), which activates antitumor NK cells and macrophages as we found in previous studies, will improve the efficacy of TIG. Aim: To test the combination of aCD40 and TIG in a mouse HR-NB model that is resistant to TIG. Methods: For these studies, we used a clinically relevant, immunologically cold, HR-NB murine model, 9464D-GD2. Syngeneic mice were intradermally injected with the tumor cells. When tumors were established, mice were randomized and treated with TIG and/or aCD40. Tumor growth and mouse survival were followed. Mice that rejected their tumors were rechallenged to test immunological memory. Changes in immune cells were evaluated by flow cytometry and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNAseq). Results: Similar to ~60% of patients with relapsed/refractory HR-NB, mice bearing 9464D-GD2 tumors did not respond to TIG. Adding aCD40 to TIG induced complete tumor regression in most mice bearing small tumors and extended survival, with many mice remaining tumor-free. The combination of aCD40 and TIG was more effective than aCD40 alone. The antitumor effect of TIG+aCD40 was not inhibited in T cell- or neutrophil-depleted mice but was substantially reduced in NK cell- and macrophage-depleted mice, indicating a role for both NK cells and macrophages in the antitumor effect. Involvement of these cells was consistent with flow cytometry and scRNAseq analyses. Mice treated with TIG+aCD40 that remained tumor-free were rechallenged with 9464D-GD2 cells and showed significantly reduced tumor growth compared to naive mice, indicating a memory response. This memory response was reduced in T cell-depleted mice, indicating the involvement of T cells in memory. Conclusion: These results show that while TIG alone was ineffective, a combination of aCD40 and TIG induced substantial tumor eradication in the 9464D-GD2 tumor model, suggesting that aCD40 may warrant future testing as an addition to the current standard TIG regimen for children with relapsed-refractory HR-NB.

papers.title: Thin2Seg: Single-cell Segmentation of Label-free FLIM at Low Photon Counts
papers.authors: Wang, G.; Nose, M.; Zhou, H.; Dmitriev, R. I.; Monaghan, M. G.; Zhang, M.
papers.abstract: Significance: Fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM) of NAD(P)H can measure the metabolism of single cells without labels. However, its weak autofluorescence requires long acquisitions that can lead to phototoxicity, while shorter acquisitions leave too few photons for current cell segmentation methods. This trade-off is aggravated in 3D live-cell models, such as spheroids and organoids, and in thin, highly adherent 2D cultures. Aim: We develop Thin2Seg to adapt a generalist segmentation network to low-photon FLIM using unlabeled recordings and a single annotated training image. The method also assesses which predicted cell masks remain stable under photon loss without additional manual annotations. Approach: We use binomial photon thinning to generate low-photon views of full-photon FLIM recordings. During training, the student network uses these low-photon views to predict the features that a teacher network extracts from the corresponding full-photon images. We evaluate Thin2Seg on macrophage and small intestinal organoid datasets against three approaches: fine-tuning on full-photon images, photon augmentation, and segmentation after denoising. We also use the predicted macrophage masks to pool photons within each cell and estimate fluorescence lifetimes. Results: Thin2Seg achieved the highest mean segmentation F1 scores among the methods tested on both datasets at median budgets of 1 and 0.5 photons per cell pixel. At these budgets, 8-12% of masks accepted by label-free certification failed the overlap criterion against full-photon predictions, compared with 14-48% of masks accepted by Cellpose's flow-error check. At 1 photon per cell pixel, 92% of annotated macrophages were recovered and 53% of lifetimes estimated were within 10% of the full-photon reference. Median cell lifetimes were within 5% of the full-photon values in 95% of macrophage images, and M2a macrophages remained distinguishable from each of the other three polarization states. Conclusions: Thin2Seg enables single-cell segmentation and lifetime analysis of label-free FLIM from much shorter acquisitions. It uses a single annotated training image and segments low-photon FLIM images directly, supporting live-cell analysis at lower photon budgets without a separate image restoration step.

papers.title: Leukocyte content accounts for most microRNA-immune associations in cutaneous melanoma: a confounder-adjusted reassessment
papers.authors: Frecha, C.; Escamilla, A.; Paz, G.; Vaca, F.; Berciano, M.; Oliver, J.
papers.abstract: Loss of antigen presentation allows tumours to escape T cells and resist immune checkpoint blockade. In melanoma cell lines, several microRNAs repress genes of the antigen-presentation machinery, and many microRNAs have been proposed as immune biomarkers in melanoma tissue. Most tissue evidence comes from bulk biopsies, in which both microRNA profiles and immune-gene expression depend on the immune-cell content of the sample. Following a pre-specified analysis plan, we regressed five immune-module scores on 662 mature microRNAs in 431 melanomas from The Cancer Genome Atlas (3,310 tests), with and without adjustment for tumour purity, leukocyte content, interferon tone and clinical covariates. We labelled each microRNA by its likely cell of origin, required target-level evidence for candidates, re-tested nine published microRNA sets, and examined the antigen-presentation programme in four skin-cancer single-cell datasets, three checkpoint-blockade cohorts (155 patients) and survival data. Of 1,334 associations significant before adjustment, 82.5% were lost after it, and 188 emerged only after it. Only 20 of the 127 microRNAs associated with antigen presentation after adjustment were labelled tumour-intrinsic, and none met the target-level criterion. The closest candidate, miR-361-5p (myeloid-suppression module), failed only a multiple-testing correction added after the target-level results were known. Published sets were enriched among unadjusted antigen-presentation associations (odds ratio 3.32) but not among adjusted ones (1.02), and lost significance as often as other microRNAs (83.3% versus 85.8%). In single-cell data, non-malignant cells expressed the antigen-presentation programme more strongly than malignant cells in 19 of 20 contrasts. A higher antigen-presentation score predicted longer survival after adjustment for composition (hazard ratio 0.69) but not for interferon tone (0.86), and the immunotherapy cohorts were uninformative. In melanoma tissue, most microRNA-immune associations reflect the immune-cell content of the biopsy. Showing that microRNAs control antigen presentation in tumour cells will require compartment-resolved measurements and adequately powered target-level tests.

papers.title: Bridging the Babble: A Method to Correlate Varying Nomenclature and Surface Marker Definitions Across the Human Splenic B Cell Literature
papers.authors: Niska, M. E.; Zhou, Q.; Burack, W. R.; Sangster, M. Y.; Zand, M. S.
papers.abstract: IntroductionFlow cytometry-based immunophenotyping is widely used for identifying memory B cell subsets associated with disease or immune responses. For simplicity, multi-feature surface marker vectors are often reduced to a single subset label for cell sorting, functional tests, and understanding immune cell interactions. Across the literature however, the same label is often used with significantly different phenotype feature vectors. Unfortunately, this babelization of phenotype definitions, makes it difficult to compare experimental results across studies. This becomes a significant reproducibility issue when cells reside in multiple anatomical compartments, with location-dependent phenotypes and naming conventions. MethodsHere, we report a broadly applicable, rigorous computational pipeline for analyzing flow cytometry data, with a novel implementation of the Jaccard Similarity Index (JSI) to compare gating schemes. The JSI is used to map the labels assigned to each cell when two gating schemes are applied to the same dataset. We designed a human splenic B cell flow cytometry panel comprising 29 B cell surface markers representative of the major gating schemes from 27 memory B cell studies, none of which used the same classification scheme. We then generated a cytometery dataset, replicated and mapped subset labels from 7 published gating schemes to each other and unsupervised clustering output. ResultsWe found that different gating schemes produced inconsistent classifications for the same cell, and clusters from different gating methods with the same label had varying levels of similarity by JSI. Using the normalized variation of information metric, we find that the overall technical similarity between gating schemes varied from 0.16 (highly dissimilar) to 0.60 (moderately similar). We found that using JSI with unsupervised clustering, and further incorporating literature-based frameworks, can help disambiguate human splenic B cell clustering results, identifying subsets described in the literature, with additional intra-subset heterogeneity. ConclusionsCluster comparison metrics, combined with unsupervised clustering and in silico replication of published gating schema enables accurate cluster comparisons across studies, increasing rigor, reproducibility, and precision. Overall, these methods enabled detailed mapping of multiple literature-based B cell subsets onto a single classification map of human splenic B cells, harmonizing predefined definitions with in-depth immunophenotyping.

papers.title: The IFN-γ Paradox: Mechanistic Modeling Uncouples Cytokine Abundance from Influenza Pathogenesis
papers.authors: Jeynes-Smith, C.; Smith, A. P.; Bruce, N.; Huang, H.-H.; Schughart, K.; Herald, M.; Smith, A. M.
papers.abstract: IFN-{gamma} has both pathogenic and protective roles during influenza infection, yet its value as a biomarker remains unclear because both increased and decreased levels associate with greater severity. To resolve this, we developed a mechanistic mathematical model of IFN-{gamma} and IFN-{gamma}-producing cell kinetics. The model was calibrated using murine data and validated against immune perturbation experiments, murine transcriptomics, human influenza challenge, and critically ill patient data. Personalizing the model with human challenge data quantified interindividual heterogeneity and generating cohorts of virtual patients with varying degrees of severity predicted unmeasured dynamics and was validated with transcriptomic and proteomic data from critically ill patients. Although severe disease was associated with greater receptor-mediated IFN-{gamma} uptake despite comparable production in non-ICU and ICU patients, early innate IFN-{gamma} signaling was a stronger determinant. These findings explain divergent IFN-{gamma} responses and establish a mechanistic framework for interpreting cytokine measurements.

papers.title: MoHuTS: Developability-Aware Antibody Humanization Using Multi-Objective Tree Search
papers.authors: Yoshimura, K.; Fujii, S.; Ishida, S.; Terayama, K.
papers.abstract: Antibody humanization aims to reduce the immunogenicity risk associated with non-human antibodies while preserving antigen binding and other properties important for therapeutic development. Identifying suitable framework substitutions often requires repeated rounds of variant construction and experimental testing, making humanization costly. Recently, machine-learning methods, including language models trained on antibody sequences, have been proposed to identify human-like framework substitutions. Although prior humanization methods have considered antigen binding and biophysical properties, it remains challenging to balance humanness across both chains with developability-related properties such as thermal stability and aggregation propensity while retaining favorable parental properties. Here, we present Multi-objective Humanization Tree Search (MoHuTS), which combines an antibody language model with reward-guided tree search to explore combinations of framework substitutions efficiently. Starting from the parental heavy- and light-chain sequences, the language model proposes successive framework substitutions. A combined score for humanness, melting temperature, a structural proxy for binding retention, and aggregation propensity guides the search. Across five computational case studies, MoHuTS generated candidates that showed favorable humanness scores and developability-related properties with relatively few framework substitutions from the parental sequences. These results suggest that MoHuTS can help prioritize humanization candidates for experimental evaluation.

papers.title: Degenerative cervical myelopathy: development and temporal validation of an interpretable machine-learning model for postoperative recovery.
papers.authors: Zhuang J, Ye Y, Liang G, Chen C, Yu T, Cheng X, Zheng X, Kang H, Liang C, Chang Y.
papers.abstract: Purpose Immune-inflammatory responses accompany spinal cord compression in degenerative cervical myelopathy. We aimed to develop an interpretable model using preoperative clinical, neurological, and hematological variables to predict 1-year postoperative recovery. Methods We retrospectively included 601 patients treated between 2018 and 2022 and divided them into training and internal validation cohorts. A temporal validation cohort included 183 consecutive patients treated between 2023 and 2024. Unfavorable recovery was defined as failure to achieve the severity-specific minimal clinically important difference in modified Japanese Orthopaedic Association (mJOA) score improvement at 1 year. Seven algorithms and 19 candidate predictors were evaluated. Data were split before imputation, with 20 imputation models fitted within training partitions. Subsequent preprocessing, predictor elimination, hyperparameter tuning, and global one-standard-error model selection used nested cross-validation within the training data. Results The final random forest (RF) model retained seven preoperative predictors: duration of symptoms, feeling of walking on cotton, clumsy hands, positive Hoffmann sign, preoperative mJOA score, monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio (MLR), and white blood cell count (WBC). The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was 0.891 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.845-0.938) in internal validation and 0.850 (95% CI, 0.794-0.906) in temporal validation. The temporal validation Brier score was 0.157, with a calibration slope of 0.855. Redevelopment without MLR reduced the AUC to 0.814 internally and 0.749 temporally. No significant differences in AUC were observed between the prespecified subgroups after Holm adjustment. Conclusion The RF model incorporating seven predictors showed consistent predictive performance across internal and temporal validation and may support preoperative risk stratification. The retention of MLR and WBC suggests that preoperative immune-inflammatory status may provide prognostic information for postoperative neurological recovery. Independent multicenter external validation is required before broader clinical use.

papers.title: PACE, Proximity-Associated Changes in Expression
papers.authors: Willie, E. S.; Rajesh Rao, S.; Ormerod, J.; Patrick, E.
papers.abstract: Cellular transcriptional states are shaped by local tissue context, yet quantifying how cellular gene expression varies with proximity to different cell types remains challenging. Cell-resolved spatial transcriptomics data are typically sparse and susceptible to contamination from neighbouring cells through diffusion, imperfect segmentation and cell overlap, making it difficult to distinguish cell-state changes from technical artefacts. We present PACE (Proximity-Associated Changes in Expression), a hierarchical empirical Bayes framework for quantifying cell-type-resolved proximity effects on gene expression. PACE uses partial pooling to stabilise inference across genes and cell types, separates contamination from biological spatial associations, and identifies coordinated transcriptional programmes underlying each proximity effect. Applied to Xenium-profiled breast cancer tissue, PACE identifies stromal cells and macrophages as the populations whose expression varies most with tumour proximity, and resolves a shift in macrophage state at tumour interfaces. In a CosMx-profiled melanoma cohort, PACE characterises previously reported outcome-associated variation in macrophage SPP1 (osteopontin) by resolving its relationship with tumour proximity across clinical outcome groups. PACE provides an interpretable framework for quantifying how tissue organisation shapes cellular state in spatial molecular data.

papers.title: A single-cell atlas of rainbow trout head kidney reveals erythrocyte-associated antiviral immunity during IHNV infection.
papers.authors: Sun J, Chen J, Zhu P, Wu J, Bai J, Kong W, Xu Z, Jiang P, Liu H.
papers.abstract: The head kidney is a central immune and hematopoietic organ in teleost fish, but the cell type-specific immune dynamics of this organ during viral infection remain poorly understood. In this study, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) to characterize the temporal immune landscape of rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss) head kidney following infectious hematopoietic necrosis virus (IHNV) infection. Head kidney cells were collected at 0, 24, 48, 72, and 144 h post-infection, and 150,024 high-quality cells were retained for integrated analysis. Unsupervised clustering identified 13 major cell populations, including neutrophils, macrophages, T cells, B cells, NK-like cells, erythrocytes, hematopoietic stem cells, thrombocytes, and kidney-associated cell types. IHNV infection induced pronounced remodeling of immune and hematopoietic compartments. Neutrophils and macrophages exhibited strong early inflammatory and interferon-stimulated gene (ISG) responses, indicating their major contribution to initial antiviral defense. B cells showed dynamic changes toward mature and plasma cell states, suggesting activation of humoral immunity. T cells displayed substantial transcriptional reprogramming, with altered pathways related to chemokine signaling, JAK-STAT signaling, T cell receptor signaling, and NF-kappa B signaling. Notably, scRNA-seq analysis showed erythrocytes expanded markedly after infection and displayed delayed induction of interferon-related transcriptional programs. Among erythroid subpopulations, mature erythrocytes showed the strongest late-stage ISG activity and upregulation of antiviral pathways, including RIG-I-like receptor, NOD-like receptor, JAK-STAT signaling, and antigen processing and presentation. Together, these findings provide a time-resolved single-cell atlas of the rainbow trout head kidney during IHNV infection and suggest that mature erythrocytes may serve as an important immunomodulatory population in teleost antiviral immunity.

papers.title: An integrative network toxicology and single-cell analysis implicates a potential myeloid-centered plaque remodeling axis in bisphenol A-related atherosclerosis.
papers.authors: Wang Q, Wu J, Qi S, Zhang J, Liu Y.
papers.abstract: Bisphenol A (BPA) is a widely exposed endocrine-disrupting chemical that has been associated with multiple cardiovascular abnormalities, yet its cell-type-specific molecular mechanisms and potential effects within the atherosclerotic plaque microenvironment remain unclear. This study aimed to systematically identify BPA-related molecular networks in atherosclerosis (AS) and characterize their potential roles within the plaque microenvironment through integrated network toxicology, machine learning, molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and single-cell transcriptomics. GSE43292 and GSE100927 were integrated as the discovery cohort for differential expression analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) to identify AS-related key genes. BPA targets predicted using ChEMBL, SwissTargetPrediction, and the Similarity Ensemble Approach (SEA) were intersected with AS key genes to obtain BPA-AS candidate targets. An ensemble of 127 machine-learning model combinations was developed using the discovery cohort, while GSE28829, GSE40231, and GSE163154 were used as external cohorts for out-of-cohort model evaluation and comparison. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), Cell-type Identification By Estimating Relative Subsets Of RNA Transcripts (CIBERSORT), molecular docking, MD simulations, and the single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) dataset GSE159677 were further applied to interpret model performance, characterize immune infiltration, assess predicted BPA-protein interactions, and investigate plaque microenvironmental mechanisms using CellChat, scTenifoldKnk, and MultiNicheNet. A total of 29 BPA-AS candidate targets were identified, mainly enriched in innate immune activation, lysosomal function, and lipid-and-atherosclerosis-related pathways. The random forest model identified 13 hub genes with good discriminatory performance, and SHAP analysis highlighted KCND3, RNASE1, HEXIM1, and TNF as major contributors to model prediction. Immune infiltration analysis revealed increased myeloid components, particularly Macrophages M0, in AS, with significant correlations with multiple hub genes. Molecular docking suggested favorable structural compatibility between BPA and several hub-gene-encoded proteins, while 100-ns MD simulations of the BPA-PLA2G15, BPA-TNF, and BPA-RNASE1 complexes provided complementary dynamic support for persistent BPA association with the predicted binding-pocket regions, despite different degrees of ligand rearrangement. Single-cell analysis further demonstrated marked myeloid enrichment in calcified atherosclerotic core (AC) samples and cell-type-specific distribution of the hub genes. CellChat identified an enhanced TNF-TNFRSF1B signaling axis in AC, while scTenifoldKnk and MultiNicheNet supported myeloid-centered inflammatory and vascular/stromal remodeling programs. Collectively, these findings suggest that predicted BPA-related targets may intersect with AS-associated inflammatory activation, lysosomal lipid metabolism, vascular remodeling, and myeloid-centered communication programs. This study provides a multilayer, hypothesis-generating framework for investigating potential molecular links between BPA and AS.

papers.title: Large-scale quantitative assessment of tissue preparation and staining conditions for robust multiplexed imaging of FFPE tissue samples.
papers.authors: Lee JL, Schaffenrath J, Wang C, Gladiseva L, Lee JJ, Wu W, Chang Y, Feng S, Nkosi D, Galván JA, Shahryari J, Yeung J, Qiu H, Yeo YY, Parmelee L, Chan CN, Cramer P, Michel H, Stephan P, Wang Y, Chong LY, Capodilupo S, Loebelenz J, Camacho Fullaway C, Liu CC, Yeong J, Einhaus J, Feyaerts D, Napier D, Basile G, Kopp N, Fantl W, Wang K, Gaudillière B, Allison D, Angelo M, Bendall SC, Loo LH, Fisher J, Rodig S, Howitt B, Ma Q, Hahn K, Jiang S.
papers.abstract: Multiplexed protein imaging or spatial proteomics enables the simultaneous measurement of over 50 proteins in intact tissues at single-cell resolution, providing insights into tissue organization and cellular interactions. However, variation in tissue preparation and staining protocols remains a major source of technical variability, limiting reproducibility and comparability across studies and platforms. Here we present a large-scale, multisite and multi-platform benchmarking study of tissue preparation conditions for formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissues. We systematically evaluated 24 combinations of antigen retrieval and antibody staining conditions using a 27-marker immune panel and ranked performance using quantitative metrics that capture signal intensity, variability and marker failure. Tris-EDTA-based antigen retrieval combined with overnight antibody staining at 4 °C consistently achieved the highest performance, whereas several commonly used alternatives showed reduced robustness. Validation across additional academic and industry laboratories and multiple imaging technologies confirmed the generalizability of these findings across tissues and platforms. We further show that marker signal intensity correlated with greater spatial heterogeneity, improving the detection of diverse cell populations. Together, our results provide practical guidelines and a standardized benchmarking strategy to improve reproducibility, harmonize workflows and facilitate cross-study comparisons in spatial proteomics.

papers.title: MtDNA Efflux Contributes to Inflammation Responses in Periodontitis via cGAS-STING-NF-κB Signal.
papers.authors: Liu J, Cheng X, Geng Y, Cao P, Zou P, Wang Y, Luan Q.
papers.abstract: Objective Despite growing evidence of the involvement of mitochondria in inflammation, the roles of specific mtDNA outside the mitochondria in periodontitis have been little explored. To address this knowledge gap, we explore the effects and mechanisms of mtDNA efflux in the development of periodontitis. Methods First, we identified the potential of HGFs as a "non-classical" component of the immune system in response to bacteria and damage-related signals using single-cell analysis. Next, we detected mtDNA efflux in HGFs and gingiva during periodontitis using immunofluorescence, adenovirus transduction, and real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction. In addition, we investigated the role of free mtDNA in periodontitis and its associated mechanisms. Results We confirmed the "immune role" of HGFs. Furthermore, lipopolysaccharide induced the upregulation of reactive oxygen species in HGFs enabling mtDNA efflux, which significantly promoted the expression and secretion of pro-inflammatory cytokines in HGFs. MtDNA efflux drives alveolar bone loss in wild-type and periodontitis mice. Mechanistically, the involvement in periodontitis of mtDNA efflux was associated with the upregulation of the cGAS-STING-NF-κB pathway. Conclusions Our findings highlight the effect of mtDNA efflux on the activation of periodontitis. Future studies focusing on the ablation of mtDNA efflux in HGFs may lead to promising treatment responses for periodontitis.

papers.title: Intercellular crosstalk and functional heterogeneity of hepatic stellate cells: A translational framework for chronic liver disease.
papers.authors: Martínez-Arroyo O, Sastre-Navarro M, Esplugues JV, Apostolova N, Blas-García A.
papers.abstract: Chronic liver diseases are a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, with hepatic fibrosis representing the common pathological pathway that can lead to cirrhosis, portal hypertension and hepatocellular carcinoma. Hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) are the principal source of myofibroblasts during liver fibrogenesis and have therefore emerged as central therapeutic targets. However, recent advances in single-cell transcriptomics, spatial omics and lineage-tracing approaches have fundamentally revised the traditional view of HSC activation as a uniform process. Instead, HSCs comprise a spectrum of phenotypically and functionally distinct states that dynamically evolve in response to chronic liver injury and differ in their contributions to extracellular matrix deposition, inflammation, immune regulation, vascular remodelling and tissue repair. During disease progression, HSCs integrate biochemical, metabolic and biomechanical cues derived from injured hepatocytes, liver sinusoidal endothelial cells, immune cells and the extracellular matrix, while simultaneously reshaping the hepatic microenvironment through reciprocal intercellular communication mediated by soluble factors, extracellular vesicles, direct cell-cell interactions and matrix-derived signals. This bidirectional crosstalk underlies both fibrosis progression and its potential regression, highlighting HSC plasticity as a defining feature of chronic liver disease. In this review, we discuss the emerging concepts of HSC phenotypic heterogeneity and intercellular communication, summarizing the molecular mechanisms that govern HSC state transitions and their interactions within the hepatic niche. Finally, we examine how these discoveries are transforming current approaches to precision anti-fibrotic therapies, providing a translational framework for the treatment of chronic liver diseases.

papers.title: Integrative network pharmacology and molecular simulation identify Brassica campestris phytochemicals targeting MIF and IDO1 in colorectal cancer.
papers.authors: Abbasi HA, Abbas MS, Iqbal N, Zafar S.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a major cause of cancer-related mortality and is strongly associated with chronic inflammation and immune dysregulation. Despite growing interest in plant-derived therapeutics, the molecular basis of the anticancer potential of Brassica campestris remains insufficiently characterized. This study used an integrated computational workflow, comprising pharmacokinetic screening, network pharmacology, a target-confidence analysis, molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and MM/GBSA scoring, to explore B. campestris phytochemicals against two immuno-inflammatory targets in CRC, macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF) and indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 1 (IDO1). Network analysis identified 69 CRC-associated targets of the phytochemicals, among which MIF and IDO1 ranked as top hub genes. Both genes were over-expressed in TCGA colorectal tumors but were not associated with overall survival. Re-querying SwissTargetPrediction retained 20-69% of the network targets (probability ≥ 0.1); because both lists derive from the same ligand-similarity method, this reflects prediction confidence and not independent validation. Docking scores ranged from - 5.2 to - 8.4 kcal/mol; 1-(2-hydroxy-1-naphthyl)ethan-1-one gave the best IDO1 score, in a heme-free receptor model in which scores and rankings changed when heme was included, whereas for MIF only ISO-1 and benzenepropanenitrile docked inside the tautomerase pocket. Re-docking of the co-crystallized ligands reproduced their poses (RMSD 1.17 Å for IDO1, in the heme-free model, and 0.86 Å for MIF). Single 100-ns MD simulations showed no ligand dissociation or large-scale structural instability. Two-frame MM/GBSA scores were calculated but, lacking replicates and uncertainty estimates, are not interpreted as binding free energies. These results are hypothesis-generating: 1-(2-hydroxy-1-naphthyl)ethan-1-one and cyclobrassinin emerge as candidates for experimental testing against MIF and IDO1, and their occurrence in B. campestris , binding and activity in CRC require experimental confirmation.

papers.title: The "death-inflammation-aging" hub in the microenvironment of degenerated intervertebral discs: New insights into macrophage phenotypic switching and multi-target therapy.
papers.authors: Jiang Y, Wang H, Qin Y, Song C, Mou J.
papers.abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IDD) represents the pathological core of low back pain (LBP), one of the leading contributors to global disability. Existing research has elaborated the roles of canonical inflammatory and immunological pathways in IDD. The discovery of three key novel regulated cell‑death modalities including ferroptosis, cuproptosis, and pyroptosis provides new perspectives for understanding the complex pathological network underlying IDD. Literature was retrieved from Web of Science, PubMed and Google Scholar for publications released from 2020 to 2025 using the keywords: back pain, intervertebral disc degeneration, macrophage polarization, ferroptosis, cuproptosis, pyroptosis. This narrative review summarizes recent evidence focusing on the interplay among macrophage polarization, inflammatory response, cellular senescence and newly-identified cell-death mechanisms in IDD. It characterizes the infiltration and M1/M2 phenotypic polarization of macrophages within the degenerative disc microenvironment, alongside their regulatory effects on extracellular matrix turnover and local inflammation. Molecular cascades and experimental evidence supporting ferroptosis, cuproptosis, and pyroptosis in IDD are summarized. Interactions between these cell-death pathways and the aging-related microenvironment that accelerate disc degenerative progression are further discussed. Multi-target intervention strategies and their translational potential are synthesized based on bioinformatics findings, in-vitro experimental observations and pre-clinical data. This review constructs a conceptual pathological framework that underpins theoretical references for precision therapy and drug development targeting IDD. Centered on the unifying pathological cascade of oxidative-stress-triggered metal-ion dyshomeostasis driving immune-inflammatory amplification, this review constructs a conceptual "death-inflammation-aging" hub framework that underpins theoretical references for precision therapy and drug development targeting IDD. Distinct from most existing reviews published between 2020 and 2025, which tend to discuss macrophage biology or individual regulated cell-death pathways in isolation, the present work emphasizes their causal, self-reinforcing crosstalk within the degenerative disc microenvironment.

papers.title: Boronic acid-directed antibody modification meets machine learning: a paper-based electrochemical sensor for dual respiratory virus antigens.
papers.authors: Yu X, Wang JX, Pang S, Cao Y, Yang HK, Jie J, Wang JH, Yang T.
papers.abstract: Respiratory infectious diseases often share similar clinical manifestations, making accurate diagnosis and timely infection control challenging. Most current sensors adopt random antibody immobilization, which reduces recognition efficiency, and lowers sensor sensitivity. Herein, we developed a boronic acid-modified electrochemical paper-based analytical device (B-ePAD) by integrating microfluidic paper-based analytical device (μPADs) with electrochemical methods. Aminophenylboronic acid was introduced to enable site-specificantibody immobilization, thereby improving antibody orientation and antigen-antibody binding efficiency. The B-ePAD enabled sensitive detection of influenza A virus nucleoprotein (IAV NP) and respiratory syncytial virus nucleoprotein (RSV NP) over linear ranges of 0.001-0.1 μg mL -1 and 0.001-0.12 μg mL -1 , with limits of detection of 0.18 and 0.12 ng mL -1 , respectively. Recoveries in spiked saliva samples were 99.6-102.0 % for IAV NP and 99.7-105.0 % for RSV NP, indicating reliable performance in complex matrices. Moreover, machine learning-enabled multifeature analysis of electrochemical signals substantially improved the accuracy of antigen concentration prediction. Benefiting from site-specific immobilization, paper-based sample handling, dual-channel electrode, and data-driven signal interpretation, the B-ePAD platform exhibited high specificity, sensitivity, and analytical accuracy, offering a promising strategy for multiplex respiratory virus antigen detection in point-of-care settings.

papers.title: Construction of a type 2 diabetes-related gene prognostic index in breast cancer and single-cell analysis of tumor microenvironment features.
papers.authors: Liang M, Deng L, Lv F, Gao P, Feng Z, Zhou J, Liao H.
papers.abstract: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) and breast cancer (BC) are epidemiologically and biologically linked; however, the extent to which T2D-related pathways influence BC prognosis and therapeutic responsiveness remains incompletely defined. In this study, we evaluated the activity of the KEGG_TYPE_II_DIABETES_MELLITUS gene set (T2DGS) in BC and found that T2DGS activity was significantly reduced in tumor tissues, whereas higher pathway activity was associated with improved overall survival (OS). We subsequently identified T2D-associated genes and constructed a T2D-related gene prognostic index (T2DRGPI), which demonstrated consistent prognostic performance in the The Cancer Genome Atlas Breast Invasive Carcinoma (TCGA-BRCA) cohort and across multiple independent validation datasets. Further analyses suggested that patients with high T2DRGPI scores were predicted to be more likely to benefit from immunotherapy, whereas those with low scores exhibited greater predicted sensitivity to several chemotherapeutic and targeted agents. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis further revealed dynamic endothelial cell remodeling within the tumor microenvironment (TME), characterized by progressive downregulation of Janus kinase 1 (JAK1) during the transition from a quiescent to an inflammatory-stress state. Moreover, in a high-glucose and high-insulin-stimulated triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) cell model, quantitative real-time PCR (qPCR) validation showed significant downregulation of JAK1 and significant upregulation of male-enhanced antigen 1 (MEA1) and family with sequence similarity 208 member B (FAM208B), suggesting that these genes may be involved in biological processes associated with T2D-related metabolic dysregulation in BC. Overall, this study reveals a potential molecular link between T2D-related pathways and BC and establishes a T2DRGPI model with potential value for prognostic stratification and therapeutic response prediction, thereby providing new insights into the clinical relevance of T2D-associated molecular features in BC.

papers.title: Single-Cell Sequencing Combined with Genome-Wide Association Studies Reveals Smoking-Associated Key Genes and Putative Downstream Injury Mechanisms in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.
papers.authors: Wang J, Wang X, Zheng W, Cao X, Wang S, Yuan J.
papers.abstract: Background Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is characterized by persistent airflow obstruction. Cigarette smoking remains a major risk factor. In this study, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) with genome-wide association studies (GWAS) to identify smoking-associated genes that are associated with the pathogenesis of COPD and to computationally infer the downstream injury mechanisms through which they act. Methods Data on COPD and smoking were obtained from public databases. Distinct cell types in COPD were identified through single-cell analysis. Next, pivotal cell populations and candidate genes were delineated by leveraging GWAS analyses linked to single-cell phenotypic characteristics, and candidate genes were identified based on expression level analysis. The biological mechanisms underlying smoking and COPD were examined using functional enrichment and immune infiltration analyses. Results Four candidate key COPD genes were identified, including SLC34A2 , SDC4 , DHCR24 , and MGST1 , which were significantly downregulated in COPD samples. Single-cell RNA-seq analysis revealed that epithelial cells represent an important cell type in COPD, with the key genes being dynamically expressed during epithelial cell differentiation. Seven specific transcription factors were identified in epithelial cells, including RFX3 , TEAD1 , IRF8 , SPI1 , IRF8 _extended, BHLHE41 , and ERG . The four key genes were significantly enriched in the "Protein degradation" pathway and the KEAP1-NFE2L2 oxidative stress pathway. In addition, 23 different immune cell types were identified, and activated B cells were negatively associated with DHCR24 , SDC4 , and MGST1 expression. Conclusion Through computational integration, we identified SLC34A2 , SDC4 , DHCR24 , and MGST1 as candidate key genes whose expression in airway epithelial cells is associated with smoking and COPD. Computational analyses suggest that these genes are involved in mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative stress. These results provide a hypothesis-generating basis for future functional studies and for examining these genes as potential biomarkers, although they do not reveal therapeutic targets.
papers.venue: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease

papers.title: NOTCH signaling and cellular plasticity in gastric cancer: A structured narrative review of the evidence, context dependence, and translational gaps.
papers.authors: Abuhassan Q, Farah H, Younis SMD, Mansurov D, Maxmudov N, Salih RM, Jaber MA.
papers.abstract: Gastric cancer remains a major global health burden, characterized by late detection, marked molecular heterogeneity, and limited durable therapeutic options. NOTCH signaling is a context-dependent pathway with both oncogenic and tumor-suppressive functions in the gastrointestinal tract, but the strength of gastric cancer-specific evidence for NOTCH-associated cellular plasticity has not been systematically appraised. In this structured narrative review, we summarize and grade the evidence on NOTCH regulation, multi-omic, single-cell and spatial observations, plasticity-associated phenotypes, therapy resistance, molecular subtypes, clinical experience with NOTCH-targeted agents and candidate biomarkers, and we separate gastric cancer data from other gastrointestinal and non-gastrointestinal studies. Gastric-specific functional evidence is largely limited to cell-line and xenograft studies linking NOTCH1/HES1- and Jagged-1-associated signaling to stem-like states, WNT/β-catenin crosstalk, EMT-like phenotypes, and resistance to chemotherapy or trastuzumab, together with correlative human studies associating NOTCH3 expression with prognosis and immune-related features. Many frequently repeated statements, including subtype-specific NOTCH alterations, NOTCH-dependent immune evasion, metabolic rewiring, and NOTCH-defined single-cell trajectories, are extrapolated from other tumor types or from pan-gastrointestinal analyses and should be regarded as hypotheses. Broad γ-secretase inhibitors have shown limited efficacy and gastrointestinal toxicity in non-gastric clinical trials, and, to our knowledge, no NOTCH-targeted treatment has demonstrated clinical benefit in gastric cancer. No NOTCH-related biomarker has been validated for diagnostic, prognostic, or predictive use. We propose an evidence-graded research agenda that prioritizes gastric-specific functional validation, subtype-resolved analyses, prospectively defined biomarkers, and early-phase trials with pharmacodynamic endpoints.

papers.title: Single-Cell Analysis of Ischemic Mouse Brain Associates Osteopontin-Related Signaling with Migration in Inflammation-Stimulated BV2 Cells.
papers.authors: Chen Y, Zang T, Yang J, Yang X, Gong Y, Lin J, Chen J, Cheng Q.
papers.abstract: Ligand-receptor inference from single-cell datasets can prioritize candidate intercellular signals but does not establish biological function. We therefore hypothesized that integrating single-cell communication inference with targeted in vitro assays could identify osteopontin-related processes associated with microglial migration after ischemic injury. Public single-cell RNA-sequencing profiles from three sham-operated and three middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) mice collected 24 h after surgery (GSE174574) were analyzed. Glial, vascular, and immune populations were annotated, microglial transcriptional changes were characterized, and intercellular communication was inferred using CellChat. Osteopontin-related communication was prioritized by integrating microglia-involved predicted interactions, cell-type-specific expression of Spp1, encoding secreted phosphoprotein 1 (SPP1; osteopontin), and Cd44, encoding CD44, disease-associated-microglia (DAM)-related transcriptional features, and feasibility of orthogonal in vitro assays. Candidate processes were evaluated in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated BV2 mouse microglial cells using quantitative reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR), a serum-gradient Transwell migration assay, and immunofluorescence. Pooled CellChat analysis identified 1,164 inferred interactions in sham samples and 1,438 in MCAO samples, with total inferred interaction strengths of 20.922 and 19.885, respectively. These pooled comparisons are descriptive and do not constitute animal-level hypothesis tests. LPS stimulation increased Spp1 and Cd44 transcripts and BV2-cell migration. Separate SPP1 neutralization and CD44-targeting treatment reduced migration and selected DAM-related transcripts. These findings associate SPP1- and CD44-related processes with BV2-cell migration and DAM-related transcriptional features under inflammatory conditions but do not establish a single causal SPP1-CD44 pathway or direct receptor activation.

papers.title: Bioinformatics and Network Pharmacology Reveal Potential Molecular Mechanisms of Taohong Siwu Decoction for Osteoarthritis.
papers.authors: Jiang Y, Luo Y, Song C, Liu Z, Fu Z.
papers.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a chronic degenerative joint disorder lacking effective disease‑modifying therapies. This study aimed to uncover hub genes and molecular mechanisms by which Taohong Siwu Decoction (THSWD) regulates inflammatory joint responses, using human OA transcriptomic data for in silico analysis and a rat model of CFA-induced inflammatory arthritis for preliminary experimental assessment. OA-related gene expression data were analyzed from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) using differential expression analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA). Network pharmacology was applied to screen THSWD bioactive constituents and corresponding targets, and intersection genes were obtained for enrichment and hub‑gene detection. Immune infiltration analysis revealed significantly altered fractions of regulatory T cells and mast cell subsets in OA synovium. Regulatory T cells and resting mast cells were increased, while activated mast cells were decreased in OA samples compared with controls. Key enriched pathways included IL‑17, PI3K‑Akt, TNF and HIF‑1 signaling, and the identified hub genes included IL6, JUN, MMP14, and PFKFB3. These findings suggest that THSWD is associated with reduced inflammatory responses in this inflammatory arthritis model through multi‑component synergy targeting immune‑metabolic networks, providing preliminary mechanistic evidence for its anti-inflammatory effects.

papers.title: Exploratory Analysis of N6-Methyladenosine Regulator Expression and Predicted Traditional Chinese Medicine-Target Associations in Ulcerative Colitis.
papers.authors: Geng H, Chang Z, Zhang Z, Xiong W, Zheng M, Meng Y, Ren J, Liu Y, Cui X.
papers.abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic inflammatory bowel disease in which m6A regulatory machinery may be associated with altered gene-expression and immune-related profiles. This exploratory bioinformatics study characterized 26 m6A regulators using GSE107499, which contains 75 lesional and 44 non-lesional colonic biopsies from subjects with UC, and examined associations with computationally inferred immune signatures and traditional Chinese medicine (TCM)-related targets. Differential expression analysis, apparent within-cohort classification, expression-based clustering, principal component analysis, single-sample gene set enrichment analysis, functional enrichment, network pharmacology, and molecular docking were performed. Twelve m6A regulators differed between lesional and non-lesional biopsies. Unsupervised analyses identified three m6A regulator expression-based clusters and two gene-expression clusters with distinct regulator-expression patterns, inflammatory-gene expression profiles, and ssGSEA-derived immune-signature enrichment scores. A PCA-derived regulator-expression summary score also differed among the identified clusters. Network pharmacology prioritized candidate herb-target and compound-target associations, and molecular docking generated candidate compound-protein interaction hypotheses. These findings are exploratory and hypothesis-generating; they do not establish clinical prediction, direct m6A modification, immune-cell abundance, target engagement, or therapeutic efficacy and require independent and experimental validation.

papers.title: Cell-in-cell structures in cancer pathology: Morphology, topology, spatial context, and clinical interpretation.
papers.authors: Lu Y, Liu Q.
papers.abstract: Cell-in-cell (CIC) structures capture interactions that can eliminate malignant cells, sustain stressed tumor cells, or alter immune attack. Their clinical meaning depends on the participating cells and the tissue in which the interaction occurs. This critical narrative review integrates original human histopathological and cytological studies with experimental and computational research identified through structured PubMed and Europe PMC searches updated to 3 November 2026. We compare established operational morphology criteria, distinguish apparent enclosure in a tissue section from demonstrated internalization, and examine how inner-outer cell identity changes prognostic interpretation. Breast cancer provides a particularly informative evidence base: studies of primary tumors, matched lymph-node metastases, treatment-exposed specimens, and lineage-resolved CIC subtypes report different associations with outcome. Across other malignancies, adverse, favorable, and null findings coexist and cannot be reconciled by a universal CIC count. Experimental studies explain this diversity through cell competition, lysosomal nutrient recovery, senescence-associated engulfment, and bidirectional interactions with immune cells. Spatial profiling and automated detection expand the questions that can be asked, while their present performance remains dependent on the specimen, annotation rules, and analytical setting. We propose a tiered research dataset anchored in morphology and sampling, with additional lineage, spatial, computational, and clinical-validation modules. The most productive clinical direction is to determine which CIC configurations identify treatment-relevant tumor behavior within a defined cancer setting, then test whether they improve decisions beyond established pathological factors.

papers.title: Multi-cohort and single-cell multi-omic analyses reveal multicellular mechanotransduction-immune remodeling in rheumatoid arthritis synovium.
papers.authors: Zhang J, Zhang P, Sun J, Zhang X, Deng L, Liu T, Wang C.
papers.abstract: Background Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) synovitis integrates immune-cell recruitment, stromal remodeling and persistent inflammation, but its relationship with tissue mechanotransduction remains unclear. We investigated whether RA involves coordinated remodeling of multicellular mechanotransduction-immune programs. Methods We constructed a 327-gene mechanotransduction compendium and used GSE89408 synovial transcriptomes from healthy controls (n = 28), patients with osteoarthritis (n = 22) and patients with RA (n = 152) for discovery. Candidates prioritized through RA-versus-Healthy and RA-versus-OA contrasts were evaluated in three patient-independent cohorts using validation-only random-effects meta-analysis. Co-expression networks, consensus clustering, locked external mapping, single-cell RNA sequencing, cell-cell communication inference, virtual knockout and single-cell chromatin-accessibility analyses (11 RA donors and one OA reference; no healthy controls) resolved network, cellular and regulatory contexts. Selected gene-expression findings were examined by quantitative PCR in independent healthy (n = 20) and RA (n = 25) synovial tissues and by overexpression and siRNA-mediated knockdown in synovial fibroblasts. Results In unadjusted bulk-tissue profiles, RA synovium showed higher expression-based scores for integrin-extracellular matrix sensing and nuclear LINC programs but lower scores for focal-adhesion force-transmission and Hippo-YAP/TAZ-associated genes. Composition adjustment attenuated several of these associations. Nine candidates met the prespecified meta-analysis criteria and mapped to four co-expression modules associated with adaptive and innate immune programs, cell cycling and mechanotransduction-related expression scores. Tissue qPCR reproduced the predicted expression directions. Two molecular states with distinct inflammatory and mechanotransduction-associated expression features were recovered in external cohorts. In exploratory analyses, TLN2 and NRXN1 expression was inversely associated with inflammatory mediators and DAS28. Exploratory single-cell analyses localized the programs to fibroblast, myeloid, lymphoid and proliferating states and inferred differences in fibroblast-myeloid communication potential. Perturbing TLN2 or NRXN1 altered selected ECM-associated transcripts and COL1A1 protein, with corresponding changes in Matrigel invasion within one donor, while transcription-factor perturbation supported candidate FOXP2-NRXN1, NFIX-NRXN1/TLN2 and FOS-TLN2 expression relationships. Conclusions Patient-derived multi-omic and experimental evidence supports coordinated transcriptional remodeling of a multicellular mechanotransduction-immune network associated with RA synovial heterogeneity.

papers.title: Decoding the human bone metastatic niche at single-cell resolution: convergent ecosystems, therapeutic vulnerabilities, and the spatial frontier.
papers.authors: Al Masri MK, Alkattan W, Ouban A, Bakir M.
papers.abstract: Bone metastases arise from biologically diverse solid malignancies but develop within a shared and highly specialized skeletal microenvironment. Recent advances in single-cell transcriptomics have enabled direct characterization of human bone metastatic lesions and have shifted the field from tumor-specific descriptions toward cross-cancer ecosystem models. Emerging pan-cancer atlases reveal partial convergence across malignancies, including recurrent suppressive myeloid states, transcriptionally defined T Cell exhaustion programs, remodeled stromal and osteolineage compartments, specialized endothelial niches, and distinct malignant-cell programs observed in bone. Several of these ecosystem features nominate candidate therapeutic vulnerabilities rather than established dependencies. Combined immune-checkpoint blockade, modulation of osteoimmune macrophage states, and disruption of stromal chemokine signaling have each received different levels of support, ranging from transcriptomic or spatial association to in vitro and in vivo perturbation, while prospective clinical validation is lacking. Because recurrence across analytical studies is not equivalent to independent replication or bone specificity, we distinguish cross-cancer recurrence from bone enrichment and from mechanistically supported skeletal-niche adaptation. Current datasets also reveal substantial heterogeneity between patients, tumor types, anatomical compartments, treatment exposures, and analytical frameworks, arguing against a single universal bone metastatic niche. This mini review synthesizes the rapidly evolving human single-cell literature on established bone metastases, evaluates candidate niche-associated therapeutic vulnerabilities, and outlines the spatial and functional validation required for clinical translation.
