papers.title: Residual inflammatory risk and the plaque immune microenvironment in coronary artery disease: evidence and limits of precision immunotherapy.
papers.authors: Han Y, Tang X, Lu Y, Men S.
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular events persist despite lipid-lowering therapy, motivating interventions against the inflammatory component of residual risk. The translational challenge is to distinguish prognostic biomarkers, causal pathways and treatment-responsive immune states. This narrative review links clinical trials with plaque biology and human single-cell and spatial studies to assess precision immunotherapy in coronary artery disease (CAD). CANTOS, COLCOT and LoDoCo2 demonstrated benefit in specific populations, whereas CIRT and CLEAR SYNERGY were neutral. Ziltivekimab lowered inflammatory biomarkers in RESCUE, while the sponsor-reported neutral ZEUS topline result underscores the need for cardiovascular outcomes. Low-dose IL-2 expanded regulatory T cells in the phase 2 IVORY imaging trial. Within plaques, retained and oxidized lipoproteins engage innate immune pathways alongside metabolic stress and diverse vascular and immune-cell states. Human datasets localize macrophage niches, microvascular interfaces and adaptive immunity, while experimental models test candidate functions. Most tissue evidence comes from carotid lesions or animal models. We evaluate IL-1β/NLRP3, IL-6 and macrophage-state pathways, then identify requirements for matching targets to patients, including plaque-focused biomarkers, coronary-relevant validation, functional perturbation and prospective trials that measure cardiovascular benefit and immune safety.

papers.title: CIPHER-Lung: retrospective exploratory internal evaluation and clinical benchmarking of an interpretable peripheral blood immune score for lung cancer prognosis.
papers.authors: Chen YY, Chang CY, Chang SC, Wei YF, Chen CY.
papers.abstract: Background Clinical Immune Phenotyping and Explainable Risk Modeling for Lung Cancer (CIPHER-Lung) is a rule-based peripheral blood immune score that organizes measured biomarkers into clinically readable concepts. We assessed whether these concepts outperform constituent markers, remain stable under assay-like computational perturbations, and identify discordance with standard disease burden. Methods This retrospective exploratory internal evaluation used 260 sample records from de-identified participants in an existing institutional cohort. Overall-survival analyses included 162 patients with lung cancer and 73 deaths, and only 31 had all six markers. The primary available-concept score combined the measured subset of a six-marker panel into four phenotypic proxies: loss of T-cell surveillance, checkpoint activation/terminal differentiation, cytokine inflammation, and hematology/myeloid inflammation. The fixed formula was applied without outcome-based coefficient refitting. Analyses included matched marker comparisons, clinical benchmarking, inverse-probability-of-censoring weighted (IPCW) evaluation, concept ablation, limited adaptation, computational jitter dropout, and 24-month discordance phenotyping. Results The available-concept score had a Harrell C-index of 0.697 and IPCW cumulative/dynamic AUROCs of 0.765 and 0.764 at 12 and 24 months. On matched participants, the composite exceeded CD3, CD8+PD-1+, CD8+CD57+, and the cytokine concept, whereas the NLR/hematology concept performed similarly in its smaller subset. The supplied fixed weighting did not outperform unweighted aggregation. Training-fold calibration and a four-concept linear probe produced only modest gains over the fixed score. Under five-point concept jitter plus 10% dropout, the median C-index was 0.691, rank correlation was 0.939, and high-risk agreement was 0.912. Descriptive point estimates were higher for clinical models. The combined model showed no material point-estimate gain over the clinical model. Paired intervals for clinical-model comparisons were unavailable. Conclusions CIPHER-Lung provides an interpretable immune-state representation supported by this retrospective exploratory internal evaluation. The score is not supported for stand-alone diagnosis, treatment selection, or replacement of stage and performance status. Candidate uses in longitudinal phenotyping, enrichment, or point-of-care reporting require complete-marker multicenter validation, documented reference standards, analytical qualification, external calibration, and prospective impact studies.

papers.title: Neuroinflammation after intracerebral hemorrhage: immune cell dynamics, molecular networks, and therapeutic implications.
papers.authors: Shao L, Mu J, Cheng X.
papers.abstract: Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) is a devastating stroke subtype whose functional outcome is largely determined by secondary brain injury rather than by the mass effect of the hematoma alone. A growing body of evidence places immune-cell-mediated neuroinflammation at the center of this secondary injury. Following vascular rupture, blood-derived damage-associated molecular patterns, heme, thrombin, and complement rapidly activate resident microglia and recruit circulating leukocytes, establishing a spatiotemporally dynamic inflammatory microenvironment. Microglia are among the earliest responders and exhibit a spectrum of functional states ranging from pro-inflammatory to reparative and phagocytic, in which the NLRP3 inflammasome and nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) signaling act as pivotal amplification hubs. Infiltrating neutrophils and their neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) aggravate blood-brain barrier disruption and perihematomal edema, forming mutually amplifying feedback loops with microglia and with the complement system. Monocyte-derived macrophages subsequently dominate hematoma clearance and inflammation resolution, while T and B lymphocytes and the complement cascade further shape the evolving immune response. Systemic inflammatory indices such as the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio hold prognostic value but are limited by sampling heterogeneity and by the distinction between association, incremental prediction, and treatment guidance. We argue that the biphasic, cell-type-specific nature of post-ICH neuroinflammation defines a series of "immune windows" that demands a shift from broad immunosuppression toward phase-specific, cell-specific precision immunomodulation. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics are refining this cellular atlas and are poised to guide next-generation, mechanism-anchored, biomarker-informed therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Synergistic and antagonistic modulation of PI3K-Akt, MAPK, and NF-κB pathways by velvet antler in osteoporosis: an integrated network pharmacology, single-cell transcriptomic, and experimental validation study.
papers.authors: Yu C, Huang H, Chen G, Li J, Zhang N, Liu W, Li F, Wu Y.
papers.abstract: Background Osteoporosis is increasingly viewed as a disorder of bone-immune crosstalk, in which the balance between osteoclast resorption and osteoblast formation is governed by interacting PI3K-Akt, MAPK, and NF-κB signalling. Velvet antler (Lu Rong, Cervus nippon ) is a traditional Chinese medicine with reported anti-osteoporotic activity but poorly defined molecular targets. Methods Drug targets (BATMAN-TCM, SymMap) and disease targets (GeneCards, OMIM, TTD) were intersected to yield core targets for PPI analysis (STRING), hub-gene identification (CytoHubba), and GO/KEGG enrichment. Diagnostic biomarkers were selected by WGCNA and three machine-learning algorithms (LASSO, SVM-RFE, Random Forest) on GSE56815 and validated in GSE7158, GSE13850, and GSE35959. Immune infiltration (ssGSEA), single-cell profiling (GSE169396; Seurat v5/SingleR), and CB-Dock2 molecular docking were performed. Predictions were then tested in primary mouse BMSCs under osteogenic induction with or without estrone (E1; 10 and 100 nM) using RT-qPCR, Western blotting, Alkaline phosphatase staining, and CCK-8. Results Twenty-eight active compounds and 1,312 core targets were identified, from which eight hub genes emerged (MAPK1, MAPK3, SRC, TP53, PRKACA, PRKACB, PRKACG, PIK3R1). A ten-gene diagnostic signature achieved an AUC of 0.947 in training and 0.838, 0.674, and 1.000 in external cohorts. Single-cell analysis of 18,916 cells localized hub and diagnostic genes to distinct populations, and docking ranked estrone-MAPK1 highest (-9.4 kcal/mol). In BMSCs, estrone promoted osteogenic differentiation, increasing ALP staining and viability with a biphasic dose response (maximal at 10 nM), alongside upregulation of Mapk1/ERK1/2 and dose-dependent downregulation of the NF-κB feedback inhibitor Nfkbia, whereas p-AKT declined rather than increased. Conclusion Velvet antler acts on the PI3K-Akt/MAPK/NF-κB network to favour osteoblast formation; experimentally, its constituent estrone promoted BMSC osteogenesis, most plausibly through MAPK/ERK rather than PI3K-Akt activation, while suppression of osteoclast activity remains a computational prediction awaiting dedicated testing. The ten-gene diagnostic panel and cell-type expression atlas reported here provide a basis for more targeted anti-osteoporotic strategies.

papers.title: TBRG4 promotes malignant progression in lung adenocarcinoma: an integrated multi-omics and experimental study.
papers.authors: Cao Y, Li P, Song L, Xing S, Zhang C, Ma H.
papers.abstract: Background Despite the identification of numerous biomarkers in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), few have been comprehensively investigated across multiple molecular and cellular dimensions. Consequently, their roles in tumor progression and tumor microenvironment remodeling remain incompletely understood. Methods Integrated multi-omics analyses were performed using transcriptomic and proteomic datasets from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA), Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO), and Clinical Proteomic Tumor Analysis Consortium (CPTAC), followed by clinical specimen validation and functional experiments, including short-hairpin RNA (shRNA)-mediated knockdown, in vitro assays, and xenograft models. Single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, immune infiltration analyses, and an atezolizumab-treated cohort were further integrated to investigate the cellular context, tumor microenvironment, and prognostic relevance of TBRG4 in an atezolizumab-treated cohort. Results TBRG4 was consistently upregulated at both the transcriptomic and proteomic levels in LUAD, and elevated TBRG4 expression was associated with unfavorable overall survival across independent cohorts. Functional experiments showed that TBRG4 knockdown suppressed LUAD cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and xenograft growth and was accompanied by reduced PI3K-AKT phosphorylation and altered epithelial-mesenchymal transition-related marker expression, supporting a potential association with these molecular programs. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses localized TBRG4 predominantly to malignant epithelial cells and revealed associations with spatial heterogeneity, epithelial-stromal communication, immune microenvironment characteristics, and increased inferred copy-number variation burden. In the atezolizumab-treated OAK cohort, elevated TBRG4 expression was associated with poorer overall and progression-free survival, although its predictive value for immunotherapy response remains to be established. Conclusions Our findings suggest that TBRG4 represents a candidate biomarker associated with malignant progression and tumor microenvironment remodeling in LUAD and provide a comprehensive multi-omics framework for future mechanistic investigation and clinical validation.

papers.title: Western and high-fat diets differentially shape the cutaneous transcriptome in imiquimod-induced psoriasiform dermatitis.
papers.authors: Albarmaqi RA, Tian Y.
papers.abstract: Background Obesity is among the most consistent comorbidities of psoriasis, yet whether different obesogenic diets aggravate psoriasiform inflammation through shared or distinct inflammatory response remains unclear. Methods We compared a Western diet (WD) and a high-fat diet (HFD) in a murine imiquimod (IMQ)-induced psoriasiform dermatitis model. Male C57BL/6 mice were fed a reference diet (RD), HFD, or WD for 12 weeks before topical IMQ, and disease severity was assessed clinically, histologically, and by qRT-PCR. To characterize diet-associated transcriptional differences, skin RNA sequencing was performed as a direct comparison between WD-IMQ and HFD-IMQ groups. Results Both WD- and HFD-IMQ increased PASI scores, epidermal thickness, and spleen index relative to RD-IMQ, with WD-IMQ skin showing the greatest epidermal hyperplasia. Although Il17a and Il23 expressions were comparable between the two obesogenic diets, transcriptomic profiling revealed distinct immune signatures. Relative to HFD, WD-IMQ skin was enriched for innate immune, complement, and acute-phase programs including genes encoding serum amyloid A proteins (Saa1, Saa2, Saa3), C3, Hp, and neutrophil-associated mediators. Conversely, HFD-IMQ skin was enriched for antigen presentation and T-cell-receptor signaling, including (Cd3d, Cd3e, Cd3g, Lat, Itk, Icos, Pdcd1). QRT-PCR validation across all three diet groups reproduced these reciprocal expression patterns. Protein-protein interaction analysis supported a divergence between the innate/acute-phase module in WD-IMQ and the adaptive/TCR-signaling module in HFD-IMQ, whereas immune cell deconvolution, being computational, was considered hypothesis-generating. Conclusions These findings indicate that different obesogenic diets elicit distinct relative inflammatory and immune transcriptional signatures during psoriasiform skin inflammation and suggest that dietary composition, in addition to adiposity, may contribute to heterogeneity in obesity-associated psoriasis.

papers.title: Multi-omics analysis and experimental validation identify ARG2 as a potential metabolic regulator linking metabolic dysregulation to inflammatory cell death in sepsis-induced acute lung injury.
papers.authors: Ji T, Liu J, Lin Y, Wen Q.
papers.abstract: Introduction Sepsis-induced acute lung injury (SI-ALI) is a life-threatening complication of sepsis that is often difficult to diagnose early due to the lack of effective diagnostic methods. Although a strong link has been established between metabolic reprogramming and immune dysfunction, the role of metabolic changes in inflammatory cell death and pulmonary immune dysregulation in SI-ALI remains unclear. Methods We analyzed transcriptomic datasets from multiple cohorts in the GEO database and applied Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) to identify pathway alterations. Three machine learning algorithms were utilized to screen for metabolism-related genes (MRGs) with diagnostic potential. To further investigate the core diagnostic gene, we performed virtual knockout analyses, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations. Finally, in vitro and in vivo experiments, coupled with lipidomic analysis, were conducted to validate gene expression patterns, functional mechanisms, and the efficacy of targeted drug interventions. Results GSEA revealed prominent changes in metabolic pathways and cell death-related processes in SI-ALI. A four-gene signature comprising ARG2, FTH1, TSC1, and GNMT was established, which demonstrated good diagnostic performance and was validated in clinical samples. ARG2 was identified as the core gene of the diagnostic signature, and its expression was positively correlated with pro-inflammatory immune cell populations in SI-ALI. Virtual knockout analyses of ARG2 revealed alterations in inflammatory pathways, particularly those related to neutrophil chemotaxis and neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation. Tacedinaline was identified as a potential ARG2-targeting compound, with interactions supported by molecular docking and dynamics simulations. Experiments demonstrated that ARG2 inhibition and Tacedinaline treatment attenuated inflammatory responses and pulmonary endothelial barrier dysfunction in vitro , while reducing lung injury and neutrophil infiltration in vivo . Additionally, lipidomic analysis showed that ARG2 knockdown reduced inflammatory responses and intracellular ceramide accumulation, suggesting an association between ARG2 and sphingolipid remodeling. Discussion Overall, we identified a novel four-gene metabolic signature with diagnostic potential for SI-ALI. Our findings indicate that ARG2 is closely associated with cell death-related processes and immune dysregulation. These results not only provide new insights into the metabolic and immune mechanisms underlying SI-ALI but also highlight ARG2 and its targeted compound, Tacedinaline, as promising avenues for therapeutic intervention.

papers.title: Potential mechanisms of active components from traditional Chinese medicine in acute myeloid leukemia via ferroptosis: an integrative bioinformatics and molecular modeling study.
papers.authors: Xie B, Chen X, Liao B, Qi Y, Chen Y.
papers.abstract: Background Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) represents a heterogeneous hematologic malignancy with divergent clinical outcomes. The prognostic significance of ferroptosis-associated genes and bioactive compounds derived from traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) in AML has not been fully characterized. We sought to construct an AML prognostic model by integrating ferroptosis-related genes with TCM molecular targets and to investigate the mechanistic basis underlying their interactions. Methods Transcriptomic data were obtained from TCGA-LAML, GSE114868 (training cohorts) and GSE71014 (validation cohort). Candidate genes were screened by overlapping differentially expressed genes, ferroptosis-related gene sets and TCM target databases. Analyses included prognostic gene selection, model construction and validation, nomogram establishment, immune microenvironment profiling, gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), Mendelian randomization (MR), molecular docking and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. Reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) was used to validate gene expression. Results CDKN1A and HMOX1 were identified as key prognostic genes, and the model showed stable predictive performance. Risk scores were correlated with age, and both genes independently predicted AML prognosis. The high-risk group had an immunosuppressive microenvironment. The two genes were enriched in ferroptosis pathways. MR analysis suggested a potential causal association between CDKN1A and AML (IVW P = 0.0104), whereas HMOX1 did not reach statistical significance (IVW P = 0.109). Quercetin and luteolin showed potential binding to the target proteins. RT-qPCR suggested lower CDKN1A and HMOX1 expression in a small AML cohort; these findings require validation in larger cohorts. Conclusion The CDKN1A and HMOX1 -based prognostic model showed potential for stratifying AML patients in exploratory analyses. TCM bioactive components may target these genes and regulate ferroptosis pathways, but these mechanisms remain hypothetical and require experimental validation.

papers.title: TRACE-Net: A Physics-Inspired Geometric Deep Learning Framework for Antibody-Antigen Docking Ranking.
papers.authors: Gong A, Bai P, Yu B, Zhan Y, Liu Y, Wu S.
papers.abstract: Elucidating antibody-antigen interactions at atomic resolution is fundamental for therapeutic antibody design. However, accurately discriminating near-native conformations from massive decoy pools remains a critical bottleneck for current high-accuracy structure prediction, as existing scoring functions often fail to capture complex interfacial interactions and monomeric deformation. To address this challenge, we present TRACE-Net, a physics-inspired geometric deep learning framework. TRACE-Net introduces three innovative modules: Context-Aware Edge Feature Recalibration (CEER), Internal Deformation-Aware Gated Fusion (IDGF), and Top-Weighted Combined Ranking Loss (TWCRL). Trained on a comprehensive data set of 1442 complexes, the model effectively reduces geometric noise and quantifies spatial divergence as a structural indicator of localized geometric deformation forced during flexible interface adaptation. Experimental results demonstrate that TRACE-Net effectively mitigates the severe ranking inversion of near-native decoys, yielding a competitive improvement in the Top-1 success rate, particularly on challenging targets. Overall, this framework offers a sensitive and informative scoring strategy for assessing predicted structures and advancing computational immunology.

papers.title: Single-cell multi-omics analyses reveal dysfunctional immune responses in patients with post-acute COVID-19 sequelae.
papers.authors: Chang, Zhu Z, Zhu R, Song Y, Xiao Z, Wu C, Li X, Zhu Y, Guo P, Liu H, Li D, Zhang H, Wang F, Su Y, Li J, Zhang M, Zhang Q, Zhao X, Liu Y, Sharma L, Xie L, Mao F, Li K.
papers.abstract: Millions of individuals experience prolonged symptoms following the acute phase of SARS-CoV-2 infection, known as post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC), but the mechanistic basis remains poorly understood. In this study, we used single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) to determine the immunological landscape of peripheral blood samples from patients with COVID-19 with viral persistence (VP) and pulmonary fibrosis (PF). In conjunction with B-cell receptor profiling and mass cytometry (CyTOF) analyses, we found that patients with VP had systemic inflammation and dysregulation of the innate immune cells, including global deficiency and dysfunction relating to antiviral activity, inflammatory responses, and antigen presentation. In contrast, molecular features were substantially different in patients with PF. Specifically, we observed evidence for an immune-megakaryocyte subpopulation expansion in patients with PF. The immune-megakaryocyte facilitated PF by expanding and reinforcing antigen-presenting activity, which emphasized the important role of antigen-presenting cells in PASC. Further, analyses demonstrated reduced T and B-cell immune activation in patients with VP and hyperactive CD4 + T and B-cell status in patients with PF. These findings illustrate the dynamic nature of both innate and adaptive immune responses during PASC development, explaining the underlying pathogenesis and illuminating potential therapeutic targets in PASC.

papers.title: Single-cell multi-omics reveals distinct immune suppression in refractory Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia.
papers.authors: Chang, Zhu Z, Hua S, Husile B, Xiao Z, Yang Z, Zhang H, Chi J, Zhu B, Xie L, Sharma L, Mao F.
papers.abstract: Mycoplasma pneumoniae infection commonly manifests as atypical pneumonia in children and generally resolves without complications. However, some pediatric patients experience severe, prolonged disease, which sometimes results in fatal outcomes. The underlying immune responses associated with refractory Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia (RMPP) remain poorly understood. Therefore, in this study, we conducted single-cell RNA-sequencing, B cell receptor/T cell receptor sequencing, and cytometry by time of flight analysis on peripheral blood mononuclear cells and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid samples from patients with RMPP, self-resolving M. pneumoniae pneumonia, and healthy controls. Our investigation revealed significant dysregulation in the peripheral circulatory immune system of patients with RMPP, potentially driven by chronic inflammation and the transition of monocytic myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs). Specifically, we observed pronounced interferon response dysregulation across innate immune cells. Moreover, the antigen presentation functions in antigen-presenting cells, particularly dendritic cells, were impaired. Remarkably, monocytes in individuals with RMPP showed considerable changes with increased expression of genes, such as SOCS3, S100A8, S100A9, and the C1q family, thus suggesting an MDSC-like transition. This phenotypic shift was exacerbated within the lung microenvironment, where CD14 + CD16 + monocytes infiltrated the tissue and differentiated into APOE + /M2 macrophages, which was triggered by CSF1, ANXA1, and TGFB1. This transition in macrophage phenotype and antigen-presenting capabilities notably hindered the activation of the adaptive immune response. Our findings reveal that patients with RMPP exhibit functional dysregulation of innate immune cells and impaired communication between the innate and adaptive immune systems. In summary, our study delineated immune dysregulation in both the peripheral blood and bronchoalveolar niche of pediatric patients with RMPP, thereby offering valuable mechanistic insights into the host response to M. pneumoniae infection and factors that contribute to refractory disease.

papers.title: Urinary 2-hydroxynaphthalene is associated with late-life poor cognitive performance and ADRM1-related microglial state alterations.
papers.authors: Ma H, Sun Q, Shi G, Feng B, Han X, Wang X, Shan A, Li S, Lian Q, Xu C, Luan H, Wen B, Guo J, Yao Q, Chen R, Sun Y, Cui T, Li C, Wei C.
papers.abstract: Introduction Environmental exposures are modifiable dementia-related risks, but population biomonitoring signals are rarely linked to Alzheimer's disease (AD) biology. Methods In 579 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2011 to 2014 adults aged ≥60 years, poor cognitive performance (PCP) was defined using Consortium to Establish a Registry for Alzheimer's Disease Animal Fluency and Digit Symbol Substitution scores. Environmental biomarkers were prioritized using complementary machine-learning methods; epidemiologic inference used survey-weighted regression and restricted cubic splines. AD-relevant contextualization included an exploratory amyloid positron emission tomography-positive AD cohort, network toxicology, docking, human-brain single-cell transcriptomics, and lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-primed BV-2 assays incorporating protein, cytokine, amyloid beta engagement assays, and a tiered transcriptional strategy composed of targeted reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction and bulk RNA sequencing. Results Urinary 2-hydroxynaphthalene (2-HN) was the only environmental analyte retained across models, showed an upper-range non-linear association with PCP, and persisted after urinary-creatinine adjustment (p for overall = 0.003; p for non-linearity Discussion Urinary 2-HN is a candidate combustion-related biomarker associated with cognitive vulnerability and implicates ADRM1-related microglial proteostasis alterations and state transitions.

papers.title: Multi-omics analysis identified ASRGL1 as a novel oncogene and potential therapeutic target in prostate cancer.
papers.authors: Ma Y, Fan R, Yu W, Duan K, Lin G, Chen Z, Li G.
papers.abstract: Background Prostate Cancer (PCa) is a globally prevalent malignancy with high heterogeneity and frequent therapy resistance. Identifying novel causal drivers and understanding their roles in the tumor microenvironment (TME) are crucial for developing new therapeutic strategies. Methods We employed an integrative multi-omics approach. First, we analyzed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data from prostate tissues to identify differentially expressed genes. Mendelian Randomization (MR) analysis was then performed using cis-expression quantitative trait loci (cis-eQTLs) and cis-protein QTLs (cis-pQTLs) from the deCODE database to infer causal relationships between gene/protein expression and PCa risk. Findings were validated using bulk transcriptomic and clinical data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) cohort. Functional enrichment, immune microenvironment analysis, and drug sensitivity profiling were conducted to elucidate the oncogenic mechanisms of the candidate gene. Results MR analysis identified asparaginase-like 1 (ASRGL1) as a novel causal risk factor for PCa (OR = 1.074, 95% CI: 1.032-1.118, P Conclusion Our study establishes ASRGL1 as a causal oncogene in PCa, linking its expression to mast cell function, metabolic reprogramming, and immune suppression. These findings nominate ASRGL1 as a promising prognostic biomarker and a potential therapeutic target, offering new insights for PCa treatment.
papers.venue: American journal of clinical and experimental urology

papers.title: Mast cells as tissue-embedded signal converters in barrier and neuroimmune networks: molecular and genetic perspectives.
papers.authors: Zhang Y.
papers.abstract: Mast cells are tissue-resident immune cells that act as versatile sources of signaling rather than solely as passive responders in IgE-mediated allergy. Recent studies have identified distinct mast cell states across epithelial, neural, stromal, metabolic, and vascular niches, with roles in anaphylaxis, host defense, pain modulation, tissue repair, and organ homeostasis. Local immune, neural, stromal, vascular, and metabolic cues, together with cell-intrinsic molecular programs, shape context-dependent mediator release and interactions with neighboring cells. This narrative review synthesizes recent evidence on mast cell heterogeneity in neuroimmune and stromal networks, with particular attention to extracellular granules, vesicular signaling, and molecular mechanisms that link tissue context to mast cell function. We further discuss how emerging single-cell and spatial technologies may help identify pathogenic or protective mast cell states and inform selective therapies that preserve beneficial mast cell functions.
papers.venue: International journal of molecular epidemiology and genetics
